classification.difficultyReason: Model an external rectangular path algebraically, substitute dimensions and reject a negative quadratic solution.

content.prompt: A rectangular lawn $a$ metres long and $b$ metres wide has a path of uniform width $x$ metres around it.

spec.description: Unshaded inner lawn and outer rectangular boundary, separated by a uniform external path. Dimension arrows show the inner dimensions a m and b m, and the right-hand path width x with a dotted leader. Decorative source blue outlines and red leader are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The lawn is a by b; the outside rectangle is (a+2x) by (b+2x). Equal inset distances represent uniform width without supplying the derived outside dimensions.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram labels are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area of the path in terms of $a$, $b$ and $x$.

answer.worked:
The outside dimensions are $(a+2x)$ m and $(b+2x)$ m. Subtract the lawn area from the outside area:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{path}}&=(a+2x)(b+2x)-ab\\A_{\text{path}}&=ab+2ax+2bx+4x^2-ab\\A_{\text{path}}&=2ax+2bx+4x^2.\end{align*}$$
The area is $(2ax+2bx+4x^2)\,\mathrm{m}^2$.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Find the area of the path in terms of $x$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: If the area of the path is $160\,\mathrm{m}^2$, find the value of $x$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4x^2+156x&=160\\4x^2+156x-160&=0\\x^2+39x-40&=0\\(x+40)(x-1)&=0\\x&=-40\quad\text{or}\quad x=1.\end{align*}$$
The width is positive, so reject $x=-40$. Hence $x=1$, giving a path width of $1\,\mathrm{m}$.

Check: $4(1)^2+156(1)=160\,\mathrm{m}^2$.
